subject: biology
title: Fertilisation, the embryo and the placenta
key_idea: Fertilisation is the fusion of the nuclei of a sperm and an egg cell. The zygote divides into a ball of cells, the embryo, which implants in the uterus lining. The placenta and umbilical cord exchange substances with the fetus, and amniotic fluid protects it.

blocks.text: A new human life starts when a sperm and an egg cell join. This section covers fertilisation and the first stages of development.

items.meaning: The fusion of the nucleus of a male gamete (sperm) with the nucleus of a female gamete (egg cell).
The single cell formed by fertilisation.
A ball of cells formed when the zygote divides.

items: A sperm enters the egg cell in the oviduct and the two nuclei fuse to form a zygote.
The zygote divides by mitosis, again and again, to form an embryo.
The embryo is a **ball of cells**. It travels to the uterus.
The embryo **implants** into the lining of the uterus, where it can be supported as it grows.
Fertilisation is the fusion of a sperm nucleus and an egg cell nucleus.
The zygote forms a ball of cells, the embryo, which implants in the uterus lining.

sections.heading: The placenta, umbilical cord and amniotic sac

blocks.text: The fetus is fed and protected by three structures. Each has its own job.

rows: Where substances are exchanged between the mother's blood and the fetus's blood. The two bloods stay separate.
Joins the fetus to the placenta. It contains the blood vessels that carry blood to and from the fetus.
A bag that surrounds the fetus and contains the amniotic fluid.
Protects the fetus from bumps and shocks, helps keep its temperature steady and lets it move.

blocks.text: What the placenta and cord exchange

items: The **umbilical vein** carries blood from the placenta to the fetus. It brings oxygen and dissolved nutrients such as glucose and amino acids.
The **umbilical artery** carries blood from the fetus to the placenta. It takes carbon dioxide and urea (excretory products) away.
Substances move across the placenta by diffusion.
The placenta also passes **antibodies** to the fetus and makes the hormones progesterone and oestrogen.
The placenta exchanges oxygen, nutrients and waste between mother and fetus. The two bloods do not mix.
The umbilical cord carries blood to and from the placenta.

blocks.text: (Supplement) The placenta is not a perfect barrier. Harmful things can cross as well as useful ones.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Substances are sorted into those that pass from mother to fetus, those that pass from fetus to mother, and those that can cross and harm the fetus.
diagram.prompt: Sort each substance by how it crosses the placenta.
groups: Can cross and harm the fetus

items: Dissolved nutrients and oxygen pass from the mother's blood to the fetus's blood.
Carbon dioxide and urea pass from the fetus's blood to the mother's blood.
Some **pathogens** and **toxins** can pass across the placenta and affect the fetus.
Syphilis and HIV are two infections that can pass from a mother to her fetus.
Useful substances and waste are exchanged across the placenta.
Some pathogens and toxins can also cross and harm the fetus.

checks.a: The nucleus of a sperm fuses with the nucleus of an egg cell to form a zygote.

checks.q: State two functions of the amniotic fluid.
checks.a: Any two from: protects the fetus from bumps and shocks, keeps the temperature steady, allows the fetus to move.

checks.q: Describe how the placenta helps the fetus to grow.
checks.a: Oxygen and dissolved nutrients diffuse from the mother's blood to the fetus. Carbon dioxide and urea diffuse the other way. The two blood supplies stay separate.

worked_example.question:
Pregnant human females have a placenta.

Describe the function of the placenta in humans.
answer_points: Oxygen passes to the fetus and carbon dioxide passes to the mother (gas exchange).
Dissolved nutrients pass from the mother's circulation to the fetus.
Excretory products pass from the fetus to the mother's circulation.
It makes a named hormone, such as progesterone.
Antibodies pass to the fetus, giving passive immunity.
It separates the fetal and maternal blood supplies.
worked_example.tip: Any four score one mark each. Name the substances that are exchanged.

worked_example.question:
A fetus develops in the uterus.

Explain how the amniotic fluid and placenta enable the safe growth of the fetus.
answer_points: The amniotic fluid prevents physical damage, because it absorbs bumps and shocks.
The placenta allows diffusion of useful substances such as oxygen, glucose and amino acids to the fetus.
It removes waste such as urea and carbon dioxide from the fetus.
It makes sure that the mother's and baby's blood do not mix.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the amniotic fluid and any two for the placenta.
